newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's Zhivkov still held on separate charges.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's Zhivkov still held on separate charges.

text.p: Bulgaria's former Communist leader Todor Zhivkov remains under house arrest on separate charges after the Sofia civil prosecutor ordered him freed in an embezzlement case, the military prosecutor said on Tuesday.

The Sofia prosecutor freed Zhivkov on Monday in connection with embezzlement charges, but he remains under house arrest on separate charges for his assimilation policy against ethnic Turks in the 1980s.
"Under my case he is under house arrest," military prosecutor Valery Parvanov told Reuters.
Zhivkov was charged in 1992 with discrimination for forcing ethnic Turks to change their Islamic names for Bulgarian ones and with curbing their religious and cultural practices.
Parvanov said the case had not been brought to trial and declined to comment on why Zhivkov, 85, was still being held.

Sofia prosecutor Mikhail Doichev said on Monday he had lifted the house arrest order linked to the embezzlement conviction following a decision from the chief prosecutor's office. "He (Zhivkov) is an old man, and in view of his health he should be free to move round town," Doichev said.
Doichev said Zhivkov had to inform the prosecutor's office if he wanted to leave Sofia or change his residence.
Zhivkov was convicted in 1992 of embezzling 21.5 million levs (then about $24 million) of public funds, spent on luxury apartments and Western cars for his family and favoured aides.
Last February the Supreme Court overturned the sentence but he still needed permission to leave his granddaughter's villa in Sofia's wealthy Boyana suburb.
Zhivkov ruled Bulgaria for 35 years until the collapse of his hardline communist administration in 1989.
A one-time associate of late Soviet leader Leonid Brezhnev and Romania's Nicolae Ceausescu, he is one of Eastern Europe's last surviving communist leaders.
